lead_headline: Restaurant tracker hits 68 active leads as three Friday additions feature Union Station sushi counter, Sloan Lake market debut, and Highlands brunch chain expansion

restaurant.blurb: 3 new leads today hold active count at 68 (33 openings, 35 closures)—opening adds edge closure count by one for first time this week. Today's openings: Ogo Korean BBQ & Sushi Pronto opens Union Station counter-service spot (chef Jackie Cho's Seoul Hospitality Group), Roll It Up Sushi debuts permanent Edgewater Public Market stall (graduation from established food truck), Mendocino Farms cuts Highlands ribbon at 3453 W 32nd (second Denver location for California sandwich chain, following this week's Union Station debut). Geographic clustering persists: Union Station accumulates sixth opening lead in 10 days (G-Que, C Burger, Mendocino, Convivio, Ogo), while Edgewater market flags first food hall addition since tracker launch. Closure side quiet—zero new shutdown detections break five-day streak of daily closure additions that built 35-lead backlog. Weekly context: 23 confirmed openings vs 11 closures suggest lead queue tilts toward delayed 2025-era closure documentation vs real-time March activity.

foreclosure.blurb: 76 filings this week surge 6% above prior week's 72 and 40% above March's 54-case floor, driven entirely by $57M Arapahoe commercial property (2038 S Vaughn) that inflates $81M aggregate—strip outlier and weekly median collapses to $317K.

liquor.blurb: Zero applications today extend March's filing drought to 27 consecutive days—now longest blackout in tracker history, erasing full month's activity vs January-February's 12/week baseline across Denver metro. April 1-7 watch window critical: if silence persists past quarterly filing deadline, signals state database lag or regulatory process disruption vs seasonal demand dip.

reputation.blurb: 4 mentions today (social chatter on motel-to-housing conversion, Sneaker Politics Fall opening, Little India closure) lift 7-day total to 60—up 62% from prior week's 37, breaking five-week 40-mention ceiling. Denver Post commands 18 pickups (30% share, down from yesterday's 37%), Instagram delivers 11, Facebook/x.com tie at 7-5. Source diversification accelerates: top source drops below one-third share for first time since tracker launch, while social platforms (Instagram/Facebook/x.com) combine for 38% vs prior week's 29%. Notable coverage: Republic Plaza loan default (Post), Politico Bar opening timeline (x.com), r/denverfood Little India shutdown thread. Week-over-week velocity sustains March's elevated baseline—four consecutive weeks above 50 mentions vs February's 35/week average.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 yesterday (1 new, 0 canceled) pushes MTD to +53 (+2.0/day), 90-day cumulative to +120 (+1.3/day). Last 7 days post +22 net (29 new, 7 canceled)—16% acceleration over prior week's +18, driven by acquisition uptick to 4.1/day from 3.4 while cancellations hold flat at 1.0/day. Two-week trend solidifies: daily new subscriber flow sustains 4+/day since March 13 (12 of 14 days hit acquisition target), offsetting churn that stabilizes near 1/day after mid-month spike. March pacing toward +55 net if final four days match current 2.0/day rate—would deliver 35% gain over February but trail early-month 2.5/day peaks as retention drag limits upside.
